A continuous pointer path from button to tooltip keeps the content visible.

Knowledge-base Markdown editor as a custom element <markdown-editor> in an open Shadow DOM. Government DMV vehicle-registration renewal modal (role=dialog aria-modal=true). Focus IS restricted to the dialog (Tab wraps among its controls), but this is the legitimate-containment carve-out: a wired, functional Esc handler closes the dialog and restores focus to the triggering button, and the focus cycle explicitly includes the focusable header Close (✕) and footer Cancel. The conformant modal the ACT corpus never models.

Cobalt Bank account-opening flow with ONE modal that is conformant containment in isolation: 'Verify your identity' opens a role=dialog aria-modal=true overlay, initial focus lands on a real focusable Close button, an Escape handler on the parent document closes it, Close/Cancel/Continue sit in the Tab cycle, and focus is restored to the opener. The defect is the embedded third-party format in the modal body: a 'SecureScan' KYC widget delivered as an <iframe srcdoc> second document whose own Tab-wrap and focusin re-grab keep focus circulating inside the frame forever, while the modal's Escape listener - living one document up - never receives keydowns fired inside the frame. A keyboard user can enter the verification step but cannot leave it.

Long-form magazine newsletter gate built with the HTML popover attribute (popover="manual"). E-commerce (outdoor retail) product 'Quick view' modal (role=dialog aria-modal=true). A focus trap cycles Tab among the size/quantity/Add-to-cart controls. The only dismiss is a round '✕' that is a <span> with role=button + aria-label and an onclick handler only — not focusable (no tabindex, not a real button) and with no keydown; there is also no Esc handler. Closeable by mouse, trapped by keyboard.

SaaS analytics dashboard 'Create alert rule' modal (role=dialog aria-modal=true). The user can see Close/Cancel but Tab can never land on them; no Esc handler either.

Government public-library 'Renew library card' modal. SaaS analytics dashboard with a valid APG role=tablist (MRR/Churn/Cohorts/Forecast). Arrows move between tabs and Tab is NOT preventDefault'd, but each tab has a blur listener that refocuses the active tab on the next tick (setTimeout(()=>tab.focus())), so pressing Tab to leave the tablist toward the panel link or the Export button instantly snaps focus back to the tab.

E-commerce headphones store with a custom div role=slider 'Max price' facet. Arrows (and PageUp/Down, Home/End) adjust the price with complete ARIA value semantics, but the thumb keydown handler also captures Tab with preventDefault() 'to prevent accidental value loss when you tab away mid-drag', with no Esc and no instruction, so focus is stranded on the thumb and cannot reach Apply, the brand checkboxes, or the product links.

Job-application form with a roving-tabindex role=listbox ('How did you hear about this role?'). Arrows navigate options and Enter selects; the keydown handler deliberately omits any Tab case, so unmodified Tab carries focus OUT to the Submit button and Shift+Tab back to the Email field. The on-screen help wrongly says 'Use Tab to move between options' — a misleading mental model, but NOT a 2.1.2 failure because Tab still exits. Boundary PASS case.

RTL Arabic article-publishing editor with an APG role=toolbar (Bold/Italic/Underline/List/Link) using roving tabindex and aria-pressed toggles. The title field and Publish button are unreachable. No Esc, no instruction.

ruleName: Developer issue tracker (Forge) label-chip list. Each chip's × opens an alertdialog confirm; confirming deletes the chip and moves focus to the NEXT chip's × (falling back to the previous chip when the deleted one was last, and to '+ Add label' when none remain). This is the F85 tag-delete exception that must NOT be flagged. Cancel returns to the chip's × (chip survives).

ruleName: Healthcare patient portal (Riverbend) medication list with per-row Remove and an alertdialog confirm. Cancel ('Keep it') correctly returns focus to the Remove trigger, but Confirm ('Remove') deletes the row, calls window.scrollTo(0,0), and focuses the first header nav link instead of the next/previous medication's controls — the logical neighbor F85 requires when the trigger is removed.

ruleName: News/editorial site (The Meridian) full-screen search overlay opened from the masthead. On open it sets aria-hidden=false and moves focus into the search input; on Escape/Close it re-applies aria-hidden=true and hides the overlay but never restores focus to the Search trigger, leaving focus unrestored (Chromium blurs the now-hidden input, so focus reverts to the document body) and the next Tab restarts from the top of the page.

ruleName: Job board / ATS profile (Hirelane) with an 'Edit profile' button opening a three-step modal wizard (Basics → Availability → Summary). Each step moves focus to its first field; the final step swaps Next for Done. Pressing Done commits the edited values, closes the wizard, and returns focus to the originating 'Edit profile' trigger — the same return as Cancel and Escape — the affirmative PASS for terminal-confirm dismissal.

The Tideline Review newsletter-signup promo (Privy/Mailchimp-style) appears over a dark scrim as a centered card. It looks modal and the developer moved initial focus into the email field, but there is NO focus trap and the background was never made inert/aria-hidden. Tabbing forward from the email field walks past Subscribe onto the article's 'Search the archive' input and button, hidden under the scrim; Shift+Tab leaks too.

Northbridge Bank 'Confirm transfer' modal (dim backdrop + centered card). A hand-rolled focus trap wraps only the FORWARD direction; the Shift+Tab branch was never written. Forward Tab is perfectly trapped, but Shift+Tab from the first control (the amount field) falls through to the browser default and lands on the page header's 'Log out' link behind the non-inert backdrop.

E-commerce seller console (Looma) orders table where every row has an identical Actions menu button (aria-haspopup/aria-expanded, role=menu/menuitem, accessible names, correct on-open focus). Three menus (rows 1,3,4) return focus to their trigger on close; the visually-identical twin on row 2 (#LG-90411) calls document.activeElement.blur() on close, dropping focus to document.body so the next Tab restarts from the sidebar nav. The page fails because of that one broken menu.

Hexagon Arena box-office 'Have a promo code?' jQuery-UI-style dialog. The developer moved initial focus in and restored it on close but never added a Tab wrap on the last control. Pressing Tab on the 'Apply code' button (the dialog's last control) follows DOM order to the page's first focusable element — a visually-hidden 'Skip to footer' skip-link — instead of cycling back to the first dialog control.

ruleName: Al-Nakheel Clinic (Arabic, lang=ar dir=rtl) 'Confirm appointment' modal. The developer hand-rolled the dialog (no native <dialog>) but did containment correctly: on open they set the background wrapper inert AND aria-hidden=true, and installed a keydown handler that wraps BOTH directions (Tab on last -> first, Shift+Tab on first -> last). In RTL the visual left/right is mirrored but Tab semantics are unchanged. Focus never escapes the modal in either direction. PASS boundary that directly contrasts case-01.

Calverton DMV 'Confirm renewal & payment' modal. The developer used the modern recommended technique — set the page wrapper's inert=true and rely on inert (no JS trap) to contain focus. But a OneTrust-style cookie-consent banner was injected by the tag manager as a direct child of <body>, OUTSIDE the inerted #page wrapper, so its 'Accept all cookies' / 'Manage' buttons stay focusable. Tab off the dialog's last control and Shift+Tab off its first control both land on the cookie buttons.
